claim: Assurant trade-in/upgrade data shows average age of traded-in Apple iPhones was 3.78 years in Q2 2024, easing to 3.63 years in Q4 2024.
scope_conditions: US trade-in transactions processed by Assurant, 2024
quoted_support: The data shows that the average age of traded-in Apple iPhones reached 3.78 years in the second quarter of 2024, then eased slightly to 3.63 years in the fourth quarter of 2024.

claim: Assurant expects the replacement-cycle length to shorten because AI features are unsupported on older hardware, pushing users to upgrade sooner.
quoted_support: Assurant also shared that they expect this number to change because of artificial intelligence. Thanks to AI, people are expected to upgrade their devices a bit faster.

claim: A UBS survey found the average iPhone in active use in the US was about 35 months old (just under 3 years), younger than the Assurant trade-in age figure.
stance_target: replacement-cycle length measurement disagreement across methodologies
scope_conditions: US installed base survey, via Investor's Business Daily citing UBS
quoted_support: Investor's Business Daily, citing a UBS survey, reported that the average iPhone in use in the US was about 35 months old — or just under three years.

claim: CIRP (late 2025) found 42% of US iPhone buyers were replacing a phone owned 3+ years, up from 32% a year earlier, while only 29% replaced a phone 2 years old or newer.
stance_target: structural lengthening of replacement cycle, against AI supercycle reset
scope_conditions: US iPhone buyer panel survey, CIRP, late 2025
quoted_support: a late 2025 report from Consumer Intelligence Research Partners (CIRP) showed that 42 percent of US iPhone buyers were replacing a phone they had owned for three years or longer, up from 32 percent a year earlier. At the same time, only 29 percent were replacing a phone that was two years old or less.

claim: The article characterizes the 2024-predicted 'AI upgrade supercycle' as having materialized as a gradual trend rather than a sharp spike, implying AI has not yet reset the replacement cycle.
stance_target: AI-driven upgrade supercycle materially resets replacement cycle
quoted_support: the massive "upgrade supercycle" predicted back in 2024 has been more of a steady climb than a vertical spike... making any shorter upgrade cycles more of a brief surge than the start of a new trend.

claim: Apple's own 'Longevity by Design' report (June 2024) states hundreds of millions of iPhones have been in active use for more than five years, and the number is growing.
scope_conditions: Apple corporate disclosure, global installed base, June 2024
quoted_support: Apple says there are hundreds of millions of iPhones that have been in use for more than five years — and that the number is still growing.
